candidates.topic: The Coldest Place in the Universe — Boomerang Nebula
candidates.teaser: There's a place in space colder than anything scientists ever manufactured in a lab — and it formed completely on its own.
candidates.video_title: This Spot in Space Is Colder Than a Lab Can Get
candidates.video_description: The Boomerang Nebula sits at just one degree above absolute zero — colder than any temperature humans have ever artificially created. Nature beat science at its own game. How is that even possible?
candidates.script: There's a place in the universe colder than any laboratory ever created — and humans had nothing to do with it. The Boomerang Nebula, 5,000 light-years away, sits at just one degree above absolute zero. That's colder than the average temperature of deep space itself. It formed when a dying star blasted gas outward at over 500,000 kilometers per hour, cooling so violently it beat every refrigerator ever built. Nature made the coldest known spot in the universe entirely by accident. Does that terrify you or fascinate you?

candidates.topic: The Grandfather Paradox — Time Travel Logic Break
candidates.teaser: Physicists found a mathematical solution to the grandfather paradox — and it makes the answer even stranger than the problem.
candidates.video_title: Physics Actually Solved the Grandfather Paradox
candidates.video_description: The grandfather paradox has baffled thinkers for decades, but physicists at the University of Queensland ran the actual numbers — and the universe may simply rewrite your actions to avoid the contradiction. Reality might be self-correcting.
candidates.script: If you went back in time and stopped your own grandfather from meeting your grandmother — you'd never be born to travel back in the first place. Paradox. But physicists at the University of Queensland ran the actual equations in 2020 and found something disturbing: the universe wouldn't let you. Your actions would automatically adjust — subtly, impossibly — to prevent the contradiction. Reality might be self-correcting, erasing your free will to protect its own logic. So the real question is: do you actually control anything?

candidates.topic: Algorithm That Predicts Death — AI Mortality Model
candidates.teaser: An AI was given patient records — and it predicted who would die within a year with unsettling accuracy, without being told what to look for.
candidates.video_title: An AI Predicted Deaths — And Doctors Can't Explain It
candidates.video_description: Researchers fed an AI millions of medical records and asked it to find patterns. It predicted one-year mortality with over 90% accuracy — using signals that no human doctor had ever thought to look for. Nobody fully understands what it's seeing.
candidates.script: Researchers gave an AI millions of hospital records and asked it to predict which patients would die within a year. It hit over 90% accuracy. The terrifying part — doctors examined its reasoning and couldn't fully understand what signals it was using. It found patterns invisible to human medicine, in data nobody thought was meaningful. An algorithm now predicts death better than the people trained their entire lives to prevent it. Should we trust it blindly — or does that make it more dangerous?

candidates.topic: The Dyatlov Pass Incident — 9 Hikers, No Explanation
candidates.teaser: Nine experienced hikers were found dead in the snow — one was missing her tongue, and Soviet investigators closed the case calling it 'an unknown compelling force.'
candidates.video_title: 9 Hikers Died. Soviets Blamed an 'Unknown Force.'
candidates.video_description: In 1959, nine trained Soviet hikers were found dead on a mountain in the Urals — some with fractured skulls, one missing her tongue, all with no external wounds. They had cut their way out of the tent from the inside and fled into minus-30 temperatures in their socks.
candidates.script: In February 1959, nine experienced Soviet hikers cut open their tent from the inside and ran barefoot into minus-30-degree snow. They were later found dead — some with fractured ribcages equivalent to a car crash, one missing her tongue entirely, yet no external wounds on anyone. Soviet investigators ruled the cause: an unknown compelling force. The case was sealed for decades. A 2019 official reinvestigation offered an answer — but eyewitnesses rejected it immediately. What would make nine trained survivalists choose certain death over staying in a tent?

candidates.topic: Ships' Graveyard — The Truk Lagoon Underwater Fleet
candidates.teaser: Beneath a calm lagoon in the Pacific, over 60 warships and thousands of human remains have sat untouched since 1944 — and the water is now one of the most biodiverse places on Earth.
candidates.video_title: 60 Warships Sank Here. Nature Took Over.
candidates.video_description: In 1944, the US Navy sank the entire Japanese fleet anchored at Truk Lagoon in just 48 hours. The ships, still loaded with tanks, planes, and human bones, never moved again. Decades later, coral colonized everything — turning a mass graveyard into one of the world's most stunning dive sites.
candidates.script: In 48 hours in 1944, the US Navy sank over 60 Japanese warships in a single lagoon in Micronesia. The ships went straight to the bottom — still packed with fighter planes, tanks, motorcycles, and human bones. Nobody moved them. Then coral arrived. Over 80 years, the entire fleet transformed into a living reef — skeletons still inside, now surrounded by thousands of fish species. A catastrophic mass grave became one of nature's greatest ecosystems. Is it a war memorial, or proof that nature reclaims everything we destroy?
